\boxed{371}

The condition means every pair of distinct vertices has at least two common neighbours, so  
\(\sum_v \binom{d_v}{2}=\sum_{\{u,v\}}|N(u)\cap N(v)|\ge 2\binom n2=n(n-1)\).  
Also \(\delta\ge3\), otherwise a vertex of degree \(\le2\) cannot share two neighbours with one of its neighbours.

Minimise \(\sum d_v\) subject to \(\sum d_v(d_v-1)\ge 2n(n-1)\) and \(3\le d_v\le n-1\).  
Because \(d(d-1)/d=(d-1)/2\) increases with \(d\), the minimum is attained by taking as many 3’s as possible and the rest as large as possible: two vertices of degree \(n-1\) and \(n-2\) vertices of degree \(3\) already give \(\sum d(d-1)=2n^2-8\ge 2n^2-2n\) for \(n\ge4\). Hence total degree \(\ge5n-8\) (and \(\ge5n-7\) when \(n\) is odd for parity), so  
\(S(n)\ge\lceil(5n-8)/2\rceil=\lfloor(5n-7)/2\rfloor\).

Equality is achieved by two adjacent hubs joined to all other \(n-2\) vertices, with those \(n-2\) vertices inducing a matching (so each has one extra neighbour). This uses  
\(1+2(n-2)+\lceil (n-2)/2\rceil=\lfloor(5n-7)/2\rfloor\) edges.

Thus \(S(n)=21,24,26,29,31,34,36,39,41,44,46\) for \(n=10,\dots,20\), whose sum is \(371\).
